description: BATTALION is tackling the Martian Map challenge at Kothamangalam. We use web development and data visualization to build an interactive survival guide for Mars.
summary:
MARSENSE is a Planetary Mission Intelligence and Decision Support System for autonomous Mars rover exploration in Jezero Crater. By unifying multi-scale NASA orbital topography (20m/px and 463m/px), surface weather, radiation logs, and mineral maps into one spatial engine, it lets planners validate landing safety, simulate survival risks, and compute optimal routes in real time.

Powered by a four-stage geospatial pipeline and eight scientific modules, MARSENSE pre-computes 2D slope gradients and 3×3 Terrain Ruggedness Index matrices for sub-second querying. It ranks landing zones (60% flatness, 40% proximity to aqueous carbonates/clays), simulates diurnal battery drain down to -83°C, dust-storm solar loss, and radiation, and runs an 8-connected A* pathfinder with a strict 15° slope cutoff.

Scientifically rich targets like ancient deltas often sit near steep cliffs and boulders. MARSENSE resolves this mathematically: trading a ~33% distance increase, its A* engine cuts peak slope from 24.8° to 8.4° for 98.5% traversability. Pre-validating traverses prevents mission-ending hardware failures, maximizes biosignature discovery, and scales for Mars Sample Return.
details:
MARSENSE is an end-to-end Planetary Mission Intelligence and Decision Support System designed for Mars rover exploration in Jezero Crater. It transforms fragmented NASA orbital and surface datasets into unified, interactive mission intelligence through a four-stage computational pipeline:

  1. Multi-Sensor Ingestion & Spatial Indexing: Fuses high-resolution Context Camera (CTX) Digital Terrain Models (20m/pixel) with wide-area Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) basin topography (463m/pixel), Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzer (MEDA) weather logs, Radiation Assessment Detector (RAD) measurements, CRISM mineralogical evidence, and atmospheric dust optical depth (Tau) indices. From these elevation grids, MARSENSE pre-computes aligned 2D slope gradients and 3x3 Terrain Ruggedness Index (TRI) matrices for sub-second spatial querying.
  2. Landing Ellipse & Biosignature Evaluation: Scores candidate touchdown zones using a weighted trade-off model (60% mechanical flatness + 40% proximity to high-value aqueous minerals such as lacustrine carbonates and phyllosilicate clays).
  3. Environmental Survival Simulation: Models diurnal thermal battery drain down to -83°C, solar array attenuation during dust storms, and cumulative ionizing radiation exposure across multi-sol missions.
  4. Hazard-Aware A* Pathfinding: Executes an 8-connected A* graph search weighted by slope angle and terrain roughness—enforcing a strict 15° critical slope cutoff—to compute safe multi-waypoint rover trajectories alongside real-time viewport hazard tiles and automated mission readiness briefs.

KEY BENEFITS

  • Quantitative Risk Reduction: Replaces manual, siloed map inspection with automated cost-surface optimization, reducing peak traversal slope from 24.8° down to 8.4° and achieving 98.5% route traversability compared to direct line-of-sight paths.
  • Real-Time Decision Speed: Pre-computed derivative matrices and spatial viewport slicing deliver sub-second hazard heatmaps, power/thermal budgets, and route recalculations as planners adjust risk tolerances.
  • Unified Situational Awareness: Consolidates geomorphology, atmospheric weather, radiation, and astrobiology onto a single interactive map interface, eliminating context switching across disconnected tools.

INTENDED IMPACT

A single wheel entrapment, rollover, or thermal power failure on Mars can prematurely end a multi-billion-dollar mission. MARSENSE safeguards robotic assets and future human explorers by quantitatively pre-validating landing ellipses and traverses. Simultaneously, it maximizes scientific return by systematically prioritizing ancient lacustrine and deltaic biosignature targets while guaranteeing safe mechanical access. Its modular, open-data architecture provides a scalable blueprint adaptable to Mars Sample Return, lunar analog planning, and autonomous planetary navigation.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE STACK

  • Languages: Python 3.12 (scientific backend and data pipelines), JavaScript, HTML, and CSS (interactive geospatial frontend).
  • Frameworks & Scientific Libraries: FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, NumPy, SciPy (spatial filtering and gradient derivation), and SQLite (metadata and target registry).
  • DevOps, Testing & Deployment: Docker (containerized deployment), uv (dependency management), Pytest (automated API, terrain, routing, and survival test suites), and GitHub Actions (CI/CD deployment to GitHub Pages).
  • Data Sources: Open NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) archives (CTX, MOLA, MEDA, RAD, and CRISM).

CREATIVITY & INNOVATION

  • Coupled Astrobiology-to-Engineering Trade-Offs: Instead of treating geological science and mechanical safety separately, MARSENSE mathematically couples them—allowing planners to visualize where high-value biosignatures sit on hazardous terrain and automatically computing the safest approach corridor.
  • Multi-Scale Resolution Blending: Seamlessly bridges coarse basin-wide MOLA context (463m) with high-detail CTX local hazard matrices (20m) so global mission planning and local wheel-level obstacle avoidance happen in one continuous workflow.
  • Interactive "What-If" Simulation: Enables users to dynamically adjust rover tilt thresholds, dust storm optical depth, and mission sol durations to immediately see how environmental stress reshapes viable routes and landing ellipses.

KEY ENGINEERING & DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS

  • Mechanical & Mobility Constraints: Enforced a 15° rover tilt cutoff and factored in micro-topographic terrain ruggedness alongside macro-slope to prevent wheel slip or high-centering.
  • Environmental & Power Survival: Accounted for extreme Martian diurnal temperature swings, dust storm solar attenuation, and cumulative ionizing radiation limits.
  • Scientific Value vs. Accessibility: Balanced proximity to aqueous mineral deposits against landing ellipse dispersion error.
  • Compute Efficiency & Portability: Used pre-computed NumPy derivative arrays, lightweight SQLite storage, and Docker containerization so complex planetary simulations run rapidly without heavy cloud infrastructure.
